item.title: NYC’s top deals: Real estate exec sells Park Ave co-op for $20M
item.description: There were 124 transactions totaling $224 million filed in New York City records in the 24 hours before 4 p.m. on Wednesday, Feb. 25, 2026. 🏆 Residential: The top home sale to hit records was in the Upper East Side, where Robert Weisz, CEO of Rye Brook, New York-based real estate firm RPW Group, and his wife Cristina Weisz parted with a co-op at 895 Park Avenue for just under $20 million. item.title: The Daily Dirt: Mamdani kicks off rental ripoff hearings
item.description: The rental ripoff hearings kick off on Thursday. Though posters for the hearings suggested more of a public brawl in an auditorium, they will be one-on-one sessions between tenants and city officials. This format was inspired by “The Mayor is Listening” event that Mayor Zohran Mamdani held at the Museum of the Moving Image in Astoria in December, said Cea Weaver, director of the Mayor’s Office to Protect Tenants. item.title: Dollars for bedrooms: Milking subsidy for maximum value
item.description: Forget “location, location, location.” Real estate is really “location, bedrooms and bathrooms.” When I bought a Brooklyn condo unit in a converted single-family brownstone, I noticed the developer had put bathrooms back-to-back in the middle of each floor. item.title: Top Connecticut broker leaves Sotheby’s for Douglas Elliman
item.description: Douglas Elliman has picked up a co-founder of one of Connecticut’s top residential teams. After three years at Sotheby’s International Realty, Megan Sullivan is joining Elliman as an individual agent. Sullivan co-founded the Greenwich, Connecticut-based Select Client Team, which ranked as the state’s top small team in 2024 with $137 million in sales, according to RealTrends. item.title: British developer Christian Candy dumps UES townhouse
item.description: British developer Christian Candy is dispensing one of his luxury residential sweets. An anonymous buyer purchased the townhouse at 8 East 62nd Street on the Upper East Side for $55 million, the Wall Street Journal reported. The undisclosed buyer was represented by Accent Holdings’ Michael Balanevsky. The sale of the 15,000-square-foot limestone townhouse breaks down to about $3,667 per square foot. item.title: Steve Roth pulls the strings of NYC’s top brokers, Koreins say
item.description: Steve Roth has such an iron grip on New York City real estate that no broker would dare to cross him for fear of losing a piece of Vornado Realty Trust’s lucrative business. item.title: Josh Gotlib, Meyer Orbach go on $380M spending spree
item.description: Josh Gotlib and Meyer Orbach are rapidly adding to the real estate investment trust they launched less than a year ago. This week, GO Residential REIT announced that it had agreed to acquire three multifamily properties in Manhattan. The firm is spending $380.5 million on the collective acquisitions, including $150.5 million to acquire the Ivy Tower from Friedman Management and $230 million to buy 411 West 35th Street and 444 West 35th Street in Hudson Yards from Maddd Equities and Joy Construct

item.title: Just 10% of NYC multifamily buildings claim 80% of evictions: REBNY
item.description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s “Rental Ripoff” hearings will begin this week, promising tenants an opportunity to complain about their landlords — directly to city officials. But a new analysis from the Real Estate Board of New York suggests that the most acrimonious living situations are in highly concentrated clusters. item.title: Genting lands January’s top loan for Aqueduct racino expansion
item.description: For real estate players seeking financing, dealmaking showed no signs of freezing in January. Lenders doled out dollars in a flurry of big-ticket deals across New York City, led by Genting’s $755 million Queens casino construction loan and SL Green’s $480 million Plaza District office acquisition loan. Hospitality, retail and even a distressed office property also found financing. Banks wrote the biggest checks for the city’s top deals, which spanned several neighborhoods in Manhattan and Queens

item.title: Mamdani’s inaugural “rental ripoff” hearing: more conference than brawl
item.description: When Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced his “Rental Ripoff” hearings, he appeared to be advertising a showdown.
